Maya: kicked off a 24h long-context loadgen against the KV runtime — seeing steady memory growth after ~6h. Retained extents climb, and one node shows paging spikes and elevated swapouts. Sharing quick notes and logs here, looking for triage ideas.

Samir: what's the run id + command?

Maya: run id load-1975-ctx24. Command: ```./loadgen --id load-1975-ctx24 --kv-mode longctx --seq-avg 4096 --seq-dist heavy-tail --rps 200 --dur 86400 --reuse-prob 0.7 --fragmentation high```

InfraBot: test-triggered: load-1975-ctx24 started on pool-kv-7 (image: rdx-2026-05-12). Tagging logs in /var/logs/perf/load-1975-ctx24/

Cheng: what's the eviction/compaction config on that pool? default LRU or adaptive? any custom retain thresholds?

Maya: eviction=adaptive-lru with target_size=75% of mem, compaction_interval=10m. Heap snapshot after ~8h: retained_extents=3120, allocated=18GB, retained=9.2GB. Jemalloc stats show active=12.1GB. Top alloc paths point to kv extent allocations + prefetch buffers.

Samir: can you capture a flamegraph and jemalloc stats (jeprof or pprof)? suspect fragmentation from repeated extent allocations + large prefetch window.

Maya: captured; pasted snippet: ``jemalloc_stats: allocated=18GB; retained=9.2GB; active=12.1GB``
Top stacks: ``runtime::kv::store::write_prefetch -> allocator::alloc_extent -> vec::reserve``
Also saw periodic spikes in vmm page-in rates aligning with eviction batches.

Olivia: on long sequences we route to the big-seq kernel which keeps larger per-request KV frames. Could be kernel selection + batching heuristics increasing the KV window. Any recent changes there? :thinking: 

Tomas: yes — last week batching changed: group_by (route, model, seq_bucket) with a 4s coalesce window. For long sequences that means more concurrent requests keep KV frames alive longer. Could amplify retained extents.

Cheng: proposed next steps: 1) add a deterministic regression to perf-suite: synthetic longctx load (heavy-tail seqs, reuse prob variants) and assert retained_extents growth bounds over 6h. e.g. retained_growth < 50MB/hour and evictions/sec stable. 2) add microbench that toggles batching window and kernel selection to measure retained footprint.

Samir: also add allocator-level microbench: deterministic RNG, repeat alloc/free patterns that mimic prefetch+fragmentation (zbench style) and compare jemalloc arenas + tcache behaviors.

Maya: I'll draft the perf test. For mitigation, enabling periodic kv.compact() every 30m reduced retained by ~20% in a 2h pilot. Not ideal but buys time.

Olivia: telemetry action: emit metrics kv.retained_extents, kv.evictions_per_min, kv.fragmentation_ratio, kv.prefetch_buffers. Alert rule: retained_growth > 100MB/hr or evictions_per_min > baseline*2.

Tomas: once Maya has a PR, we'll run the regression on dedicated pool-kv-regen (no other noise) and try the batching window flip (+/- 2s) and kernel rollbacks. Ping me when ready.

Maya: thanks — drafting PR and test harness now. Will include run id, seed, and exact loadgen flags for reproducibility. cc @Samir @Cheng for review. :eyes:
